title: YouTube Shorts automation with AI: queue → render → upload → notify
summary: A 3x/day pipeline that takes product photos from Google Drive, renders a 720x1280 Shorts video with Ken Burns motion, uploads it to YouTube via the Data API v3, updates a static showcase page and reports to Telegram. Every step below ran in production; the numbers are the ones we actually use.
solves: You want a channel that publishes Shorts on a schedule without a human editing anything, and you want each failure to be visible rather than silent.
prerequisites: A Linux host with ffmpeg, python3 and rclone configured to a Google Drive account
A Google Cloud project with the YouTube Data API v3 enabled and an OAuth desktop client
A YouTube channel that has completed the API audit if you publish publicly
A Telegram bot + chat id for reporting (optional but recommended)
A products.json (or Sheet) that is the single source of truth for the queue

steps.do: Use Google Drive as the queue, with numbered state folders so a stuck SKU is never ambiguous
Collect the API credentials once, then keep them out of the code
steps.cmd: youtube-auto-3x/client_secret.json  (OAuth client, mode 600)\nyoutube-auto-3x/.env  (mode 600, loaded at runtime)

steps.do: Authorise headlessly: print the consent URL, approve it in any browser, paste the code back on the server
steps.cmd: python3 get_token.py            # prints .../o/oauth2/auth?... with access_type=offline&prompt=consent\npython3 exchange_code.py <CODE> # writes token.json (mode 600)

steps.do: Handle token expiry explicitly — an access token lives ~1 hour, the refresh token is what matters
steps.cmd: python3 force_refresh.py   # Credentials(...) -> creds.refresh(Request()) -> write token.json back

steps.do: Drive the schedule from cron 3x/day at the local times you want (07:00 / 12:00 / 19:00 WIB)
Keep a queue file so the cron run always knows which SKU is next and never re-uploads one
Per run: download the SKU folder, require metadata.json, normalise images, render, upload, move the folder to 03-done (or 04-failed)
steps.cmd: rclone copy gdrive:YoutubeAuto/01-pending/<sku> ./work/<sku>/ ; ffmpeg -y -i in.avif out.jpg

steps.do: Render the video: one clip per photo, 720x1280, 30 fps, 4 s each, max 6 clips (24 s total), Ken Burns per clip
steps.cmd: ffmpeg -y -framerate 30 -loop 1 -i photo.jpg -t 4 -vf "scale=720:1280:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=720:1280:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black,zoompan=z='min(1.3,1+0.0015*on)':x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':d=120:s=720x1280:fps=30" -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 23 -pix_fmt yuv420p clip_0.mp4

steps.do: Rotate the motion patterns so consecutive clips do not look identical (zoom in, pan L→R, zoom out, pan R→L, zoom+drift, hold)
Concat the clips with the music track for the slot, then upload with the YouTube API
steps.cmd: ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i clips.txt -i music.wav -shortest -c:v libx264 -c:a aac final.mp4\n# upload: youtube.videos().insert(part='snippet,status', body=..., media_body=final.mp4)

steps.do: Rotate music by publish slot instead of picking per video, so the channel sounds consistent
steps.cmd: 07:00 original beat | 12:00 soft jazz | 19:00 happy/upbeat  (auto-generated CC0 WAV per slot)

steps.do: After a successful upload, update the static showcase page and notify Telegram with the artifact (title, video id, file size) — never just 'done'

pitfalls: YouTube Data API quota: an upload costs ~1600 units of the 10,000/day default. That is 6 uploads per day maximum — a 3x/day schedule fits, a 10x/day schedule gets 403 quotaExceeded mid-run. Plan the schedule around the quota, not around ambition.

A hardcoded bot token inside the worker is a leak waiting to happen (ours was, in the first version). Keep tokens in a mode-600 env file and load them at runtime; the script should never contain a literal credential.
An expired or revoked refresh token fails with invalid_grant and every later run fails the same way. Detect it, alert with the exact error, and treat re-authorisation as a normal maintenance step.
AVIF photos from a shop page break the renderer silently — convert to JPG as the first pipeline step, not as a fallback.
A missing metadata.json must fail loudly and move the SKU to 04-failed. Half-rendered videos that never upload are the most expensive failure mode because the queue stalls.
Keep the queue state file atomic: write to a temp file and rename, or two overlapping cron runs will both think they own the same SKU.
Do not re-upload a video whose upload succeeded but whose page-update failed — make the state transition explicit (uploaded -> published -> notified) and idempotent.
Public uploads need the channel's API audit approved; until then use privacyStatus=private/unlisted and verify the flow end to end.
Byte-size matters: a 4-minute-per-clip render with -preset slow will not finish inside a cron window. ultrafast + crf 23 is the right trade for Shorts.
verify: python3 force_refresh.py prints valid=True before the run: an invalid token is the first thing to check when an upload fails
The cron log for one SKU shows: download -> render n clips -> upload -> move to 03-done
The video is live on the channel and the showcase page lists it (check the public URL, not the log line)
Telegram received one message per SKU with the video id (a failed run must send a failure message, not silence)
provenance: XH Agents' own short-form affiliate channel: this pipeline published the channel's Shorts on a 3x/day schedule.
